svg.aria-label: L10 Shared L2 lineage: sectored lines, distance banks and insertion by class
svg.text: L10 Shared L2 lineage: sectored lines, distance banks and insertion by class
Left, three published ideas redrawn. Right, the M1 L2 from the measurements and the patents. Between them, what was kept, changed and added.
Seznec 1994, Fig. 3; Kim, Burger and Keckler 2002, Fig. 1; Qureshi 2007 and Jaleel 2010, section 4
M1 shared L2, 12 MiB, 12 ways, 128 B lines
measured; cachelets and insertion from patents
a sectored cache: one tag, several lines, a valid bit each
a non uniform cache: the near banks answer sooner
Kim: S-NUCA maps a line to one bank by index
D-NUCA lets hot lines migrate nearer
where a new line enters the recency stack
new lines at LRU, a few at MRU
a long interval, promoted on a hit
Qureshi: a scan that enters at LRU cannot flush the working set
Jaleel: a two bit interval per line learns the same thing
the insertion stack follows the text of both papers, not one figure
a valid bit per sub line
a sector is exactly two L1 lines
four static banks, one per core
class bits ride with the L1 victim
one 128 B line is two 64 B halves, each on its own
four 3 MiB cachelets; a core sees the near one at 17 cycles
the 3 and 7.5 MiB steps are measured
which bits pick the cachelet is a patent reading
where a victim from the L1 enters the twelve way stack
measured: 12 MiB, 12 ways, 128 B, 17 cycles, inclusion, per core LRU
patents: cachelets, the three bits, the loser bank
open: a pinned sweep per hash class, four curves or one
